hook: Ivan Zhang studied computer science at the University of Toronto, graduating in 2016, and worked as an engineer across biotech and MLOps roles before co-founding the research collective for.ai in 2017. In 2019 he co-founded Cohere alongside Aidan Gomez and Nick Frosst, building the company into an enterprise-focused large language model provider. As co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, Zhang has overseen technical product development at Cohere and worked closely with the company's public sector and government customers. For.ai, the research group he started before Cohere, was later folded into Cohere as its open research division, Cohere Labs. He has co-authored research spanning generative adversarial networks, model regularization and AI safety.
name: Ivan Zhang

reading.body:
Ivan Zhang co-founded Cohere in 2019 to build large language models for enterprise customers, combining technical depth from MLOps roles with research foundations established at for.ai in 2017.

Zhang's path reflects the structure of modern AI infrastructure: academic training in computer science, applied engineering work in adjacent domains, and then focused founding. His move from for.ai into Cohere as co-founder and CTO shows how open research collectives can serve as technical incubators before folding into commercialized product companies. For.ai became Cohere Labs, its research division, suggesting a deliberate strategy to preserve research capability within the commercial entity.

Cohere's focus on enterprise customers and public sector work positions it in the market segment serving organizations building AI systems rather than consumers. This matters for compute and infrastructure because enterprise deployments at scale drive sustained demand for model access and inference capacity, creating the foundation for long-term infrastructure investment. Zhang's co-authorship on AI safety research, particularly work on mitigating harmful outputs, indicates technical leadership engaged with safety constraints rather than pure capability scaling.

The data does not reveal Cohere's capital structure, compute allocation, or power consumption patterns. It documents leadership background and research interest but not the company's actual infrastructure choices or constraints.
